subject: TransitX trial rescope and ownership alignment
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@transitx.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@transitx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + draft POC plan

Hi Samir / Laura — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a first-pass POC plan attached so we can align on scope and acceptance criteria before engineering kicks off.

Key outcomes from the call:
- Two priority workflows: 1) Customer support triage and response suggestion (primary), 2) Knowledge search for internal docs (secondary).
- Target evaluation window: 4 weeks of active testing after initial integration.
- Procurement asked for SOC 2 evidence and a simple SOW for internal approval.

Draft success criteria (proposal):
- Latency: p95 generation latency under 250ms for <256-token completions in the hosted trial environment.
- Accuracy: >72% correct routing or correct first-draft reply on our seed test set (judged by TransitX SMEs).
- Coverage: Successful resolution rate across the 6 seed intents >= 65%.
- Cost target: average token cost projected not to exceed $0.015 per token with our suggested batching + caching profile.

Attachments: [Attachment: transitx_poc_plan_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 420 KB)]

Ask / next steps:
- Samir: confirm the two workflows above and whether you want to include ticket routing as a third use case (I thought you were leaning yes on a follow-up).
- Laura / procurement: indicate any mandatory evidence/doc template we should fill out for your procurement review.
- Ben / Marissa: can you confirm owners for integration and instrumentation? I propose Ben own commercial coordination and Marissa lead SRE/SE integration work.

I'll wait for confirmation and will circulate an updated plan with a timeline.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + draft POC plan

Tessa — quick internal note before I loop back to TransitX. Two items from my side:

1) Use-case add: during the call Samir suggested ticket routing (auto-tag + team routing) as a potential high-value quick win. If we add routing we should re-baseline success criteria (routing accuracy target of 80% on seed labels) and add a short synthetic evaluation dataset. That will change instrumenting requirements (we need labeled ticket exports).

2) Timeline impact: adding routing pushes our active testing window from 4 weeks to 5 weeks (1 week extra for data mapping and label verification). We should surface that as an optional "Scope+Routing" path so procurement and the engineering sponsor can decide.

Marissa — can you estimate SE hours for routing integration (data mapping + validation + 1 e2e test)? I want to call out owners and rough effort in the updated plan.

I'll draft two labeled timeline options for Samir: (A) core 4-week POC (search + reply); (B) 5-week POC including routing.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — useful summary. Confirmations and clarifications below: 

1) We definitely want ticket routing included. That is a primary scoring dimension for our ops team. Routing accuracy should be treated as the leading success metric — we can agree on 80% on seed labels as Ben suggested.

2) Timeline: procurement wants the SOW and SOC2 evidence by end of next week (11 Jun) in order to approve dedicated test credentials. Can Redwood share your SOC2 cert and a one-page compliance summary to speed approvals?

3) Data: we can provide a 3-week export of representative tickets and a small set of annotated examples (approx 500 labeled rows). We'll need guidance from Marissa about format and fields.

4) Cost sensitivity: our finance lead expects a cost projection for a 5-week trial (including the routing workload) that maps to your batching strategy. If possible provide a delta between 4-week (core) vs 5-week (routing) so we can evaluate.

If you can update the plan with an explicit "Scope A / Scope B" choice and send back the compliance artifacts, procurement will expedite.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of AI, TransitX

Folks — I put together an updated evaluation plan and a success matrix based on Samir's routing ask. See attachments and summary below.

Summary of changes (v2):
- Two scope tracks:
  * Scope A (Core): knowledge search + response suggestion — 4-week active test. Acceptance: p95 latency < 250ms, >=72% correct suggestions, coverage >=65%.
  * Scope B (Core + Routing): adds ticket routing. Active test 5 weeks. Acceptance: routing accuracy >=80% on TransitX seed labels; other metrics same as Core.
- Ownership:
  * Integration SE: Marissa Cole — data ingestion, schema mapping, instrumentation (logs + simple tracing hooks).
  * Commercial / kickoff owner: Ben Carter — procurement liaison, SOW sign-off, billing.
  * Success / QA: Rishi Malhotra — evaluation rubric and weekly scoring.
- Effort estimate:
  * Scope A: SE ~ 2.5 days (integration + smoke tests).
  * Scope B: SE ~ 6 days (data mapping + labels ingestion + routing validation).

Attachments: [Attachment: transitx_success_matrix_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 75 KB)], [Attachment: poc_timeline_v2.csv (text/csv, 3 KB)]

Action items I will do this week:
- Share a CSV template for ticket export and a short config checklist for ingestion.
- Produce a short evaluation rubric (Rishi will finalize thresholds).

Ben / Tessa — I recommend we send Samir a single updated plan that includes both tracks and a clear ask for which scope they prefer by EOD Friday (11 Jun) so procurement can stay on schedule.

Marissa
